headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/network workflows between gpt-researcher and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; Plandex reads/writes the project directory and applies staged changes. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if research output is fed into coding tasks. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is copied into Plandex prompts or plan files, injected instructions can influence code actions.
IF Plandex ingests research artifacts as trusted text, malicious content in those artifacts can steer tool use.
mitigations: Keep research outputs and coding prompts in separate directories.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex for any task sourced from research text.
Manually strip instructions from imported documents before reuse.
Use a fixed template that treats external text as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images, while Plandex reads and writes the project directory with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from A into B and then out through B's model/provider calls. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, files read by gpt-researcher can be exposed to Plandex.
IF Plandex sends project contents to a model provider, any sensitive data in shared files can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace.
Remove secrets and personal data from shared folders.
Turn off automatic file inclusion where possible.
Review outbound prompts before model submission.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read the filesystem, and Plandex can write files and modify git state while gpt-researcher can spawn subprocesses and use broad network egress. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide without locking. Because the profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no orchestrator lock, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF Plandex auto-applies while gpt-researcher is generating artifacts, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones.
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock file.
Disable auto-apply during concurrent runs.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a content-writing/research agent that can produce citations and reports, and Plandex is a coding agent with review-then-apply behavior. If Plandex treats research output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes. The profiles do not show a verification barrier by default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Plandex uses gpt-researcher reports as factual input without verification, incorrect claims can be turned into code changes.
IF research citations are copied into implementation tasks, downstream actions may rely on unverified facts.
mitigations: Require a human check before applying research-derived changes.
Ask Plandex to restate assumptions before editing files.
Cross-check citations against source documents.
Limit research output to summaries, not directives.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states a residency or certification mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets while Plandex can transmit project contents to external model providers, but the profiles do not prove a regulated-data violation. One-agent citations are sufficient because the mismatch is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared project files, Plandex may transmit it to a model provider.
IF the deployment requires strict residency or retention controls, external API use can violate policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Use self-hosted model endpoints where available.
Redact secrets before handing files to either agent.
Check retention settings on external providers.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency boundary.
